Assume Countable Choice. Let $T$ be a densely defined linear operator on $H$.

- $T$ is **symmetric** when $T\subseteq T^*$, that is, $D(T)\subseteq D(T^*)$ and
  $Tx=T^*x$ for all $x\in D(T)$; equivalently
  $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y\in D(T)$.
- $T$ is **self-adjoint** when $T=T^*$, that is, the domains and the values
  agree.
- $T$ is **essentially self-adjoint** when its closure $\overline T$ is
  self-adjoint; by [[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]] this presupposes
  that $T$ is closable.

**Consequences, with proofs.** These are part of the content of the definition.

1. *A symmetric $T$ is closable.* $T\subseteq T^*$ and $T^*$ is closed
   ([[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]]), so $T^*$ is a closed
   extension of $T$. In particular the closure $\overline T$ exists and
   $\overline T\subseteq T^*$.
2. *The closure of a symmetric operator is symmetric.* If $T\subseteq T^*$,
   the inclusion reversal of
   [[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]] applied to
   $T\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq T^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$. Applying it once more to the inclusion
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq(T^{**})^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^{***}$. Since $\overline T=T^{**}$ and
   $(\overline T)^*=T^{***}$
   ([[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]]), this reads
   $\overline T\subseteq(\overline T)^*$: the closure is symmetric. (Each
   application is legitimate because the adjoint is defined once its operator
   is densely defined, and $D(T^{**})$ is dense because
   $T\subseteq T^{**}=\overline T$, so that $D(T^{**})$ contains the dense
   domain $D(T)$.)
3. *A self-adjoint operator has no proper symmetric extension.* If $T=T^*$ and
   $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*$, then $S^*\subseteq T^*$ by inclusion reversal,
   so $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*\subseteq T^*=T$ and all inclusions are
   equalities.
4. *A self-adjoint operator is closed*, being equal to the adjoint $T^*$ of the
   densely defined $T$, and *an essentially self-adjoint operator has exactly
   one self-adjoint extension*, namely $\overline T$: a self-adjoint extension
   $S$ of $T$ is closed, hence contains the least closed extension
   $\overline T$, and then $S\subseteq S^*\subseteq(\overline T)^*=\overline T$
   by item 2 and symmetry, so $S=\overline T$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product $(\cdot,\cdot)$ linear in
the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let
$V\subseteq H$ be a dense linear subspace carrying a Hilbert norm
$\|\cdot\|_V$ whose inclusion $V\hookrightarrow H$ is continuous
([[lem-w-one-two-is-a-hilbert-space]]; the standard instance is
$V=H^1_0(\Omega)\subseteq H=L^2(\Omega)$). A sesquilinear form
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb C$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in
the second ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), is a
**closed sectorial form** on $V\subseteq H$ if:

(i) $a$ is **bounded on $V$**: there is $C<\infty$ with
$|a(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ for all $u,v\in V$;

(ii) there are $M\ge0$ and $\theta\in[0,\pi/2)$ with
$$\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)\ge-M\|u\|_H^2,\qquad |\operatorname{Im}a(u,u)|\le\tan\theta\,\bigl(\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+M\|u\|_H^2\bigr)$$
for every $u\in V$;

(iii) $V$ is complete for the **shifted form norm**
$$\|u\|_{a,M}^2:=\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+M\|u\|_H^2+\|u\|_H^2,$$
By (ii) the square is
nonnegative and $\|u\|_H\le\|u\|_{a,M}$, so $\|u\|_{a,M}=0$ only for $u=0$;
condition (iii) is the closedness of the form. The Hermitian pairing $b(u,v)=(a(u,v)+\overline{a(v,u)})/2+(M+1)(u,v)_H$ has $b(u,u)=\|u\|_{a,M}^2>0$ for $u\ne0$, so it is an inner product and this expression is its norm ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]).

**Comparison with a prescribed form-domain norm.** Under Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), $\|\cdot\|_{a,M}$ is equivalent to $\|\cdot\|_V$. The upper bound is $\|u\|_{a,M}^2\le(C+(M+1)\|\iota\|^2)\|u\|_V^2$. The identity in the reverse direction has closed graph: convergence in either norm implies convergence in $H$, so the two limits agree. Both normed versions of $V$ are Banach, and [[thm-closed-graph-theorem]] makes this inverse identity bounded, giving a positive lower comparison constant. Generation results below may instead take this norm equivalence as an explicit hypothesis, retaining only Countable Choice for Lax–Milgram.

The **associated operator** $A$ of such a form, in the $e^{tA}$ sign
convention, is
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{u\in V:\ \exists\,f\in H\ \text{with}\ a(u,v)=-(f,v)\ \text{for all}\ v\in V\Bigr\},\qquad Au:=f .$$

The vector $f$ is unique, so $A$ is well defined: if $f,g$ both satisfy the
relation, then $(f-g,v)=0$ for every $v\in V$; since $V$ is dense in $H$ and
the inner product is continuous, $(f-g,w)=0$ for every $w\in H$, and testing
$w=f-g$ gives $\|f-g\|^2=0$. The operator $A$ is linear
([[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]],
[[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]]): if $u_1,u_2\in D(A)$
with associated vectors $f_1,f_2$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb C$, then
$a(u_1+\lambda u_2,v)=a(u_1,v)+\lambda a(u_2,v)=-(f_1+\lambda f_2,v)$ for all
$v\in V$, so $u_1+\lambda u_2\in D(A)$ with $A(u_1+\lambda u_2)=f_1+\lambda f_2$.
The defining relation reads
$$\langle Au,v\rangle=-a(u,v)\qquad(u\in D(A),\ v\in V),$$
and is the only sign convention used on this page.

The form is **coercive** with constant $\alpha>0$ when
$\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)\ge\alpha\|u\|_V^2$ for all $u\in V$. A coercive
form is closed: (iii) holds with explicit estimates, since (i) and coercivity
give, with $\iota:V\hookrightarrow H$ the inclusion,
$$\alpha\|u\|_V^2\le\|u\|_{a,M}^2\le\bigl(C+(M+1)\|\iota\|^2\bigr)\|u\|_V^2 .$$

### Sign convention

The dictionary $\langle Au,v\rangle=-a(u,v)$ fixes the orientation: for
$u\in D(A)$ the quadratic form of $A$ is the negative of $a$,
$$\langle Au,u\rangle=-a(u,u),$$
so the sector condition (ii) says that the shifted operator $M-A$ is
accretive,
$$\operatorname{Re}\langle (M-A)u,u\rangle=\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+M\|u\|_H^2\ge0 ,$$
and gives $\operatorname{Re}\langle (A-M)u,u\rangle\le0$ for every $u\in D(A)$.
This is the convention in which $e^{tA}$ solves $u'=Au$ and the resolvent
sector of $A$ opens to the right; the opposite pairing
$a(u,v)=\langle Au,v\rangle$ is the Pazy-Lunardi convention for $-A$ and is not
used here.

### Coercivity versus sectoriality

A coercive form satisfies (ii) with $M=0$ and $\theta=\arctan(C/\alpha)$ at
most, because $\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)\ge\alpha\|u\|_V^2\ge0$ and
$|\operatorname{Im}a(u,u)|\le C\|u\|_V^2$. The sectorial condition is a
one-sided quantitative hypothesis on $\operatorname{Re}a$ and
$\operatorname{Im}a$ along the diagonal; the phrase "elliptic operator" is
never used as a hypothesis ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with
spectral projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). The **discrete
spectrum** $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ is the set of eigenvalues of $A$ that are
isolated points of $\sigma(A)$ and whose eigenspace is finite dimensional; the
**essential spectrum** is
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A):=\sigma(A)\setminus\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A),$$
with $\sigma(A)$ as in [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]].

For $H=\{0\}$ use its unique PVM directly: the spectrum and both parts
are empty and every projection has rank zero. Below suppose $H\ne\{0\}$,
as required by the cited spectral theorem.

**Spectral-projection description, with proofs.** Fix $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and write
$P_\varepsilon:=E((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ for
$\varepsilon>0$.

Here rank means the algebraic dimension of the range when finite; rank
$=\infty$ means the range is not finite dimensional. The calculus
[[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] gives the support facts:
$E(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$, and every open interval about a
spectral point has nonzero projection. Projections on disjoint sets have
orthogonal ranges, and $E(B)E(C)=E(B\cap C)$
[[def-projection-valued-measure]].

1. *$E(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$.* If
   $x=E(\{\lambda\})x$, its scalar measure $E_x$ is supported on
   $\{\lambda\}$ by the projection identity. Thus
   $\int\mu^2dE_x=\lambda^2\|x\|^2<\infty$, so $x\in D(A)$, and
   $$\|(A-\lambda)x\|^2=\int|\mu-\lambda|^2dE_x=0.$$
   The domain and norm identities are supplied by the unbounded calculus and
   [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]. Hence $Ax=\lambda x$.
   Conversely, for an eigenvector (or the zero vector) the same norm identity
   gives zero integral. On $\{|\mu-\lambda|\ge1/n\}$ this bounds the measure
   by $n^2$ times that zero integral; taking the countable union shows
   $E_x(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$.
   Since $\|(I-E(\{\lambda\}))x\|^2$ equals this scalar measure,
   $E(\{\lambda\})x=x$.
2. *A finite-rank interval contains only finitely many spectral points.*
   If $P_\varepsilon$ has rank $r<\infty$ and its interval contained $r+1$
   distinct spectral points, choose disjoint small open intervals about those
   finitely many points, all contained in the given interval. Each has a
   nonzero projection by support. Choose one unit vector in each range.
   They are orthonormal vectors in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$, hence
   linearly independent (take inner products with each vector), contradicting
   its dimension $r$. Thus there are at most $r$ spectral points there.
   In particular any $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$ with such a finite-rank
   $P_\varepsilon$ is isolated: take a smaller interval around $\lambda$
   excluding the other finitely many points. For that interval the projection
   is $E(\{\lambda\})$ by support, is nonzero by support, and has finite rank
   since its range lies in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$. By item 1,
   $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity.
3. *The two rank characterizations.* If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$,
   an isolating interval has projection $E(\{\lambda\})$, of finite rank
   by item 1. Conversely, if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue and some
   $P_\varepsilon$ has finite rank, item 2 proves it discrete. Hence
   $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue and some }P_\varepsilon\text{ has finite rank}.$$
   If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, item 2 excludes every finite-rank
   interval. Conversely, if every $P_\varepsilon$ has infinite rank, each is
   nonzero, so support puts $\lambda$ in $\sigma(A)$, and the just-proved
   discrete characterization excludes it from $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$.
   Therefore
   $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon=\infty\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0.$$
4. *$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ is closed.* If $\lambda_n\in
   \sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ and $\lambda_n\to\lambda$, then for every
   $\varepsilon>0$ some $n$ has $(\lambda_n-\varepsilon/2, \lambda_n+
   \varepsilon/2)\subseteq(\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon)$, so
   $\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon\ge\operatorname{rank}P_{\varepsilon/2}^{(n)}
   =\infty$ and $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ by item 3.

The closure conclusion is in $\mathbb R$, and also in $\mathbb C$ since
$\mathbb R$ is closed there. A spectral accumulation point has infinitely
many spectral points in every surrounding interval, so item 2 forces infinite
rank. An isolated eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity has its infinite-dimensional
eigenspace inside every interval range by item 1. Consequently an accumulation point of $\sigma(A)$ and an isolated eigenvalue of
infinite multiplicity both lie in $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, and $\sigma(A)$
is the disjoint union of $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ and
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Work on a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable. Let $A$ be self-adjoint and let $B$ be symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and
$A$-bound less than one ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).
Then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is self-adjoint. If $A$ is merely essentially
self-adjoint and $B$ is symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and $A$-bound less
than one, then $A+B$ on $D(A)$ is essentially self-adjoint and its closure is
the self-adjoint operator obtained by applying the first part to $\overline A$
and the graph-norm extension of $B|_{D(A)}$ to $D(\overline A)$. If $A\ge\gamma$ and
$(a,b)$ is an admissible pair for $B$ with $a<1$, then
$A+B\ge\gamma-\max\{a|\gamma|+b,\ b/(1-a)\}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space H with spectral
projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ and let $H_{\mathrm{pp}}$,
$H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}$ be the subspaces of
[[def-pure-point-absolutely-continuous-and-singular-continuous-spectral-subspaces]].
Then $H_{\mathrm{pp}},H_{\mathrm{ac}},H_{\mathrm{sc}}$ are closed, mutually
orthogonal, $T$-reducing subspaces with
$$H=H_{\mathrm{pp}}\oplus H_{\mathrm{ac}}\oplus H_{\mathrm{sc}},$$
canonically determined by $T$; the restrictions of $T$ to them are
self-adjoint and their spectral measures are respectively purely atomic,
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and atomless and
singular. If $H$ is separable and $\mu$ is a maximal scalar spectral measure
with disjoint Borel supports $B_{\mathrm{pp}},B_{\mathrm{ac}},B_{\mathrm{sc}}$
of its discrete, absolutely continuous and singular continuous parts, then
$H_{\mathrm{type}}=\operatorname{ran}E(B_{\mathrm{type}})$.

Here a support means a Borel carrier (zero mass off the set), not necessarily topological support. A maximal scalar spectral measure is a finite positive Borel measure mu with $E_x\ll\mu$ for every x (in particular a scalar spectral measure with this domination property qualifies). The last assertion is conditional on the supplied mu. On the zero Hilbert space use the unique PVM and full-domain zero operator directly.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$, let $\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, let $H_0=-\Delta$ and $H=H_0+M_V$ on $D(H)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and define

$$\Omega_\pm=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_0}.$$

These wave operators exist by the concrete Cook construction. Write $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)$ for the closed span of the eigenspaces, $\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}(H)=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)^\perp$, and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H),\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)$ for the absolutely continuous and singular continuous spectral subspaces: locally define $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}=\{u:\mu_u\ll dE\}$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}=\{u:\mu_u\text{ is atomless and singular to }dE\}$ for the PVM constructed by [[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-separable-spectral-calculus]]. Then:

(a) $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_\pm\subseteq\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$;

(b) each wave operator individually is asymptotically complete:

$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_+=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_-=\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=\mathcal H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_+^*\Omega_-$ is unitary on $\mathcal H$ and commutes with $e^{-itH_0}$ for every real $t$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^d)$ be a map of class $C^2$ into the
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices, let $P(s)$ be the spectral projection of $H(s)$
for a spectral cluster $\sigma_P(s)$ that is separated from the complementary
spectrum by a uniform gap: $\operatorname{dist}(\sigma_P(s),\sigma(H(s))\setminus\sigma_P(s))\ge g>0$
for all $s\in[0,1]$. Require that the cluster is followed coherently:
$P(s)$ is continuous in operator norm (equivalently, it follows the local
Riesz continuation of its initial cluster). Fix $T>0$. Let $U_T$ solve
$i\,\partial_sU_T(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$, $U_T(0)=I$
by the finite matrix construction below, and let
$U_A$ solve $i\,\partial_sU_A(s)=\bigl(TH(s)+i[P'(s),P(s)]\bigr)U_A(s)$,
$U_A(0)=I$ (equivalently $U_A'=(-iTH+K)U_A$ with $K=[P',P]$). Then:

(a) $P\in C^2([0,1];\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d))$ and $K=[P',P]$ is
anti-Hermitian of class $C^1$ with $[K,P]=P'$.

(b) There is a $C^1$ Hermitian $X:[0,1]\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d)$ with
$[H(s),X(s)]=K(s)$ for all $s$.

(c) *Intertwining.* $P(s)U_A(s)=U_A(s)P(0)$ for all $s$.

(d) *Adiabatic estimate.* With
$C:=2\sup_s\|X(s)\|+\int_0^1\bigl(\|X'(s)\|+\|K(s)\|\|X(s)\|\bigr)ds$ one has
$$\bigl\|(I-P(s))U_T(s)P(0)\bigr\|\le\frac CT\qquad(s\in[0,1]).$$

The estimate is finite-dimensional and conditional on the uniform positive gap;
gap-closing families and unbounded families are not covered.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$L\to M$ be a smooth complex line bundle with a supplied Hermitian metric and
Hermitian connection $\nabla$. Write $\Omega_\nabla$ for its curvature and
$c_1(L):=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for the published integral line class, using the
complex orientation on the underlying real plane. Let
$$\rho_M:H^2(M;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^2(M;\mathbb R)$$
be induced by $\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Under the natural de Rham
isomorphism $J_M$,
$$J_M\left[ -\frac{\Omega_\nabla}{2\pi i}\right]=\rho_M(c_1(L)).$$
For a disconnected base the same line-class convention is understood on each
component; the global class is the Euler class displayed above.

If $\nabla'$ is any complex connection on $L$, not necessarily metric
compatible, then
$$\left[-\frac{\Omega_{\nabla'}}{2\pi i}\right]=\iota_M\!\left(J_M^{-1}\rho_M(c_1(L))\right)\quad\text{in }H^2_{\rm dR}(M;\mathbb C),$$
where $\iota_M$ is induced by including real-valued forms into complex-valued
forms. Thus the arbitrary-connection class is identified with the same real
class by the degree-one transgression.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension $d\ge0$,
let $n\ge0$, and let $E:=V^{\otimes n}$ carry the commuting left place action
of $S_n$ and diagonal action of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$
([[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]]). Let
$B:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{g^{\otimes n}:g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\}$,
and for $\lambda\vdash n$ put
$$M_\lambda:=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_n}\bigl(S^\lambda,E\bigr),$$
on which $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts by postcomposition
$(g\cdot\psi)(s):=g^{\otimes n}\psi(s)$ and $B$ acts by
$b\cdot\psi:=b\circ\psi$. Then:

1. **(Decomposition.)** There is an isomorphism of
   $(S_n\times\operatorname{GL}(V))$-modules
   $$E\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n,\ \ell(\lambda)\le d}S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,$$
   where $S_n$ acts on the first factor and trivially on $M_\lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts on $M_\lambda$ by postcomposition and trivially
   on $S^\lambda$. The sum runs over exactly the partitions $\lambda\vdash n$
   with at most $d$ rows.
2. **(Nonzero irreducible factors.)** For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). $$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. Let $d,e\geq1$ and let $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ be complex-linear. Choose the standard input basis $(|i\rangle)_{i=1}^d$, let $E_{ij}=|i\rangle\langle j|$, and use the ordered tensor convention input-reference $\otimes$ output. Define the (unnormalized) Choi matrix

$$J(\Phi):=\sum_{i,j=1}^{d}E_{ij}\otimes\Phi(E_{ij})\in M_d(\mathbb C)\otimes M_e(\mathbb C).$$ Then $\Phi$ is completely positive if and only if $J(\Phi)\geq0$, and this holds if and only if there are $q\leq de$ matrices $K_1,\ldots,K_q:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^e$ such that $$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a=1}^{q}K_aXK_a^*\qquad(X\in M_d(\mathbb C)).$$

The empty sum is allowed when $\Phi=0$. For any such Kraus representation, $\Phi$ is trace-preserving if and only if $\sum_{a=1}^{q}K_a^*K_a=I_d$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\ge1$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), with adjoints as in [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]] and the finite trace as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Recall that an endomorphism $F$ is an **effect** when $F\ge0$ and $I-F\ge0$, i.e. $0\le F\le I$ in the quadratic-form order ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).

(a) *Definitions.* A finite POVM is a finite family $(F_a)_{a=1}^p$, $p\ge1$, of effects with $\sum_aF_a=I$. An **instrument** here is a finite family $(M_{a,r})_{1\le a\le p,\,1\le r\le q_a}$ of endomorphisms of $H$, where each $q_a$ is a non-negative integer; its outcome operators and update maps are $F_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}$ and $I_a:\operatorname{End}(H)\to\operatorname{End}(H)$, $I_a(R):=\sum_rM_{a,r}RM_{a,r}^*$, with empty sums equal to zero. It is **normalized** when $\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I$. For a normalized instrument the $F_a$ are its **outcome effects**, as proved in (b); without normalization they need not be effects.

(b) If $(F_a)$ is a finite POVM and $\rho$ a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]) then $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)\ge0$ and $\sum_ap_a=1$. If $(M_{a,r})$ is a normalized instrument then the $F_a$ form a finite POVM, $\operatorname{tr}I_a(\rho)=p_a$, each $I_a(\rho)$ is non-negative, and whenever $p_a>0$ the normalized update $I_a(\rho)/p_a$ is a density operator.

(c) *Ideal Lüders case.* For an orthogonal projection $P$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]]) put $M_0=P$, $M_1=I-P$. Then $\sum_jM_j^*M_j=P+(I-P)=I$, the effects are $F_0=P$, $F_1=I-P$, and $I_j(\rho)=P\rho P$ or $(I-P)\rho(I-P)$.

(d) *Non-determination.* Effects alone do not determine the update: there are two normalized instruments on $\mathbb C^2$ with the same outcome effects $F_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $F_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ whose updates differ on the same input.

$$A_+(f)=\overline{S_+(f)}=S_-(f)^*,\qquad A_-(f)=S_+(f)^*=\overline{S_-(f)}$$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],

Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]]. Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ a nonempty compact interval, $\hbar>0$, and $\mathcal H:I\to\mathcal B(H)$ a norm-continuous family of bounded self-adjoint operators. Put $A(t)=-i\mathcal H(t)/\hbar$ and $K=\sup_{t\in I}\|A(t)\|<\infty$. For every $s,t\in I$ define $U_0(t,s)=I_H$ and, recursively, the oriented Bochner integrals
$$U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_s^t A(r)U_n(r,s)\,dr,$$
where $\int_s^t=-\int_t^s$ when $t<s$. Equivalently, for $s\le t$ these are the **latest-time-left** ordered integrals
$$U_n(t,s)=\Bigl(\frac{-i}{\hbar}\Bigr)^n\int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}\mathcal H(t_n)\cdots\mathcal H(t_1)\,dt_1\cdots dt_n,$$
with the simplex integral meaning the nested integral with $t_n$ outermost and $t_1$ innermost. For arbitrary $s,t$ its unambiguous nested form is $\int_s^t dr_1\int_s^{r_1}dr_2\cdots\int_s^{r_{n-1}}dr_n\,A(r_1)\cdots A(r_n)$. Then:

(a) $\|U_n(t,s)\|\le(K|t-s|)^n/n!$ for all $n\ge0$ and all $s,t\in I$.

(b) $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_n(t,s)$ converges in operator norm uniformly on $I\times I$, is jointly norm-continuous, satisfies $U(s,s)=I_H$, and obeys $\|U(t,s)-I_H\|\le e^{K|t-s|}-1$. In particular all original forward-time convergence claims hold.

(c) For every $s,t\in I$,
$$U(t,s)=I_H-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^t\mathcal H(r)U(r,s)\,dr.$$
For fixed $s$ this is the unique continuous $\mathcal B(H)$-valued solution on $I$. More generally, the solution with initial value $C\in\mathcal B(H)$ at $s$ is $U(t,s)C$. For $a<b$, the operator-norm derivatives are
$$\partial_tU(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\mathcal H(t)U(t,s),\qquad \partial_sU(t,s)=+\frac{i}{\hbar}U(t,s)\mathcal H(s),$$
with the corresponding one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. Therefore, for every $\psi\in H$, $U(t,s)\psi$ is strongly continuously differentiable in either variable and satisfies the same equations applied to $\psi$, with the common bounded-generator domain equal to all of $H$.

(d) Every $U(t,s)$ is unitary, $U(t,s)^*=U(s,t)=U(t,s)^{-1}$, and
$$U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)\qquad(r,s,t\in I).$$
These conclusions include both orientations of the time interval and intervals containing positive and negative times. If $a=b$, all terms with $n\ge1$ vanish and $U(a,a)=I_H$; the derivative assertions then have no nontrivial interval on which to apply.

No separability hypothesis on $H$, invariant domain for an unbounded operator, differentiability of $\mathcal H$, spectral theorem or physical interpretation is required.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: A densely defined symmetric closed form q≥−c on a complex Hilbert space determines a unique self-adjoint H≥−c with Q(q)=D((H+c)^(1/2)) and q(u,v)=⟨Hu,v⟩ on D(H)×Q(q). If real v satisfies |v[u]|≤a q0[u]+b||u||² for q0≥0 and a<1, q0+v is closed and semibounded on Q(q0).
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Apply Riesz to q+(c+1)⟨.,.⟩ to construct bounded positive injective resolvent; invert on its range and use spectral calculus. Prove shifted form norm equivalence for perturbation.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For semibounded self-adjoint H, λk=inf_dim L=k sup_||u||=1,u∈L qH[u], with L⊂Q(H), equals the kth eigenvalue below inf σess(H), counted with multiplicity, or that threshold if fewer exist. Compact form embedding gives a complete discrete eigenbasis.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Prove spectral projection dimension bounds directly from the PVM; compact embedding gives compact shifted resolvent and use compact self-adjoint spectral theorem. Do not apply finite real Courant-Fischer to an unbounded complex operator.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For real W≥0 bounded and compactly supported on R³ and κ>0, Kκ=W^(1/2)(−Δ+κ²)^(−1)W^(1/2) is compact positive. The multiplicity of eigenvalue −κ² of −Δ−W equals that of 1 for Kκ; the number of eigenvalues below −κ² equals the number of eigenvalues of Kκ above 1.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Kernel e^(−κ|x−y|)/(4π|x−y|) gives Hilbert-Schmidt compactness; intertwine eigenvectors, then compare negative form subspaces through (−Δ+κ²)^(1/2).

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For self-adjoint H0, g∈H and real λ, let Hλ=H0+λ|g⟩⟨g|. With R0(z)=(H0−z)^(−1) and 1+λ⟨R0(z)g,g⟩≠0, Rλ=R0−λ R0|g⟩⟨g|R0/(1+λ⟨R0g,g⟩). Zeros below σ(H0) give bound states when g≠0.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Multiply the proposed inverse on both sides on D(H0); use spectral measure derivative and monotonicity for eigenvalue count.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For self-adjoint H0,H on separable Hilbert spaces and bounded identification J, define Ω±=s-lim_t→±∞ e^(itH)J e^(−itH0)Pac(H0) where it exists; completeness means ran Ω±=Hac(H), and S=Ω+*Ω−. Two-space identifications and excluded bound sectors are explicit.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For real bounded compactly supported V on R³, H=−Δ+V on H² has complete Ω± relative to −Δ, no singular continuous spectrum, and S is unitary on free L². Positive-energy stationary scattering agrees with the wave-operator scattering matrix with the retained normalization.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Consume actual repaired compact-support completeness and stationary-dynamical identification carriers; prove compatibility of any changed Fourier convention and restrict all stationary claims to k>0.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: If S(E)∈U(r) is C¹ on an energy interval, Q(E)=−iℏ S(E)*S′(E) is Hermitian, tr Q=−iℏ d log det S/dE, and under energy-independent unitary channel changes Q transforms by conjugacy.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate S*S=I and determinant; an energy-dependent basis adds a connection term, which must be retained. This algebraic theorem does not prove an operational arrival-time interpretation.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: If the scalar m(z)=⟨(H0−z)^−1g,g⟩ has a specified analytic continuation across an open absolutely continuous interval, noncancelled zeros of 1+λm_cont(z) give poles of the corresponding continued rank-one resolvent matrix elements. These poles are not complex eigenvalues of self-adjoint Hλ.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a∈S(R^(2d)) and ε>0 define OpεW(a)u(x)=(2πε)^−d∫e^(i(x−y)·ξ/ε)a((x+y)/2,ξ)u(y)dy dξ on Schwartz functions. For normalized u∈S define $W_\varepsilon[u](x,\xi)$=(2πε)^−d∫e^(−iy·ξ/ε)u(x+y/2)overline(u(x−y/2))dy.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For Schwartz symbols and states, ⟨OpεW(a)u,u⟩=∫a $W_\varepsilon[u]$; ∫$W_\varepsilon[u](x,\xi)$dξ=|u(x)|² and the position integral is the ε-Fourier momentum density. Wε is real but need not be nonnegative.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For each d there are a fixed integer Nd and Cd such that a∈C∞(R^(2d)) with bounded derivatives through Nd gives ||OpεW(a)||≤Cd∑_|α|≤Nd ||∂αa||∞, 0<ε≤1.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Prove with phase-space cube partition, integration by parts and almost orthogonality; choose Nd=4d+4 as a sufficient nonoptimal index. This is a new local prerequisite, not an already accepted supplier.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a real quadratic h and its self-adjoint Weyl realization, Uε(t)*OpεW(a)Uε(t)=OpεW(a∘Φt), a Schwartz, where Uε=e^(−it Op(h)/ε) and Φt is the Hamiltonian flow. For h=|ξ|²/2+V(x), V smooth with all derivatives of order≥2 bounded, compact time intervals and compactly supported smooth a, an operator-norm O(ε²) remainder follows from an explicitly proved order-zero symbol estimate and cubic Moyal commutator remainder.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Quadratic commutator is exact on S; integrate Heisenberg equation and extend boundedly. The nonquadratic branch requires a NEW local bounded-symbol lemma and cubic remainder, both specified in prose; it is not supplied by measure-theoretic Egorov.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a C² family of rank-r orthogonal projections P(x) on C^d over a smooth parameter manifold M, E={(x,v):P(x)v=v} has Hermitian fibers and projected connection ∇=P d. Along a C² path P(s), Kato transport solves W′=[P′,P]W, W(0)=I.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For the projected connection of a C² rank-r projector family, F=P(dP∧dP)P. In a local orthonormal frame V with V*V=I, A=V*dV is anti-Hermitian and Fframe=dA+A∧A; under V→Vg, A→g^−1Ag+g^−1dg and F→g^−1Fg. Kato transport is unitary and P(s)W(s)=W(s)P(0).
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate P²=P to obtain PdPP=0; expand ∇² and use the local frame identity. Differentiate W*W and W*PW.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a C² rank-one projector on an oriented closed smooth surface, (i/2π)∫tr F is an integer equal to the first Chern number in this anti-Hermitian connection convention; local geometric phase is exp(−∮A), including transition functions when a path crosses frame patches.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For C² finite Hermitian H(s) with a coherently followed spectral cluster separated by a uniform energy gap g>0, iℏ∂sUT=T H(s)UT transports the cluster up to leakage ≤ℏ C/T using X solving [H,X]=[P′,P]. For a simple eigenvalue, the comparison evolution factors into exp(−iT∫E ds/ℏ) and Kato geometric transport.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Rescale the actual finite adiabatic supplier H→H/ℏ or T→T/ℏ; compute constants with energy units and use its intertwining evolution. Derive scalar phase by projecting the equation.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: On (C^d)^⊗N the permutation representation and diagonal U(d) action admit an orthogonal decomposition into Specht factors and multiplicity spaces indexed by partitions λ of N with at most d rows. Every permutation operator acts in the Specht factor; every collective U(d) action acts in the multiplicity factor.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Start from exact published Schur-Weyl decomposition; choose invariant inner products by finite-group averaging and restrict GL(d) to U(d). Identify the finite commutants; no parastatistics assignment follows.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For N≥2 spin-half factors define si as adjacent swaps and ei=I−si=2Psinglet_(i,i+1). Then ei²=2ei, ei e_(i±1) ei=ei, and [ei,ej]=0 for |i−j|>1. This is a *-representation of TL_N(2), not a claim of faithfulness at all N.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Check swap eigenvalues on singlet/triplet; compute contraction on three spinors using the normalized singlet. Tensor with identity to extend the local identity.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: On a finite spin-half chain with dimensionless σ, Si=ℏσi/2 obeys Si·S_(i+1)=ℏ²(si/2−I/4)=ℏ²(I/4−ei/2). Therefore a finite exchange Hamiltonian ∑Ji Si·S_(i+1)/ℏ² is a Hermitian TL element commuting with global SU(2), with energies obtained independently in finite Schur-Weyl blocks.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use σaσb=δabI+iεabcσc and evaluate on singlet/triplet; retain Ji in joules and finite chain. The physical identification of exchange is an additional effective model.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: The unordered configuration space of two distinct points in R² is homeomorphic to R²×(0,∞)×RP¹, hence its fundamental group is Z. Its one-dimensional unitary representations send the elementary exchange to e^(iθ), and a full winding to e^(2iθ). Bosonic/fermionic assignments θ=0,π are selected cases.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use center of mass, relative radius and relative angle modulo π; lift the angle to R and classify loops by winding. The flat line bundle is built from the universal cover quotient with that character.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Assuming AC, a nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system on a finite-dimensional real symplectic space with fixed nonzero central parameter is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger system. Regularity, finite dimensionality and irreducibility are necessary hypotheses of this planning interface.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use actual current draft Stone–von Neumann carrier and its Mackey closure as draft planning suppliers; carry AC and do not infer infinite-mode uniqueness.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For m>0 on L²(R^d), T(a)f(x)=f(x−a) and B(v)f(x)=e^(imv·x/ℏ)f(x) satisfy B(v)T(a)=e^(imv·a/ℏ)T(a)B(v). Direct sums with distinct masses have distinct central characters.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Multiply the two explicit unitary maps, prove strong continuity by dense smooth vectors, and identify the commutator scalar.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: A spin-s irreducible unitary SU(2) representation has central element −I acting by (−1)^(2s); its ray action descends to SO(3). Half-integral spin gives a projective SO(3) action and integral spin an ordinary one.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use highest-weight spin basis and the 2π z-rotation eigenvalues e^(−2πim); show all m have the same parity.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For H=⊕_(j=1)^r Hj and allowed bounded observables A=⊕Aj, expectation tr(ρA) equals tr((∑PjρPj)A). Off-diagonal sector coherences are operationally invisible relative to that chosen algebra.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Block multiplication and trace cyclicity; this is an algebra-relative theorem, not a proof that every mass coherence is forbidden.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For finite completely positive maps Ia:M_d→M_e with ∑Ia trace preserving, there is an isometry V:C^d→C^e⊗C^q and mutually orthogonal register projections Qa with ∑Qa=I such that Ia(ρ)=TrE[(I⊗Qa)VρV*(I⊗Qa)].
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Apply existing Choi-Kraus theorem outcome by outcome, attach distinct |a,α⟩ basis vectors and check V*V=I. Do not duplicate the existing general instrument theorem.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Two finite PVMs {Pi},{Qj} admit a joint POVM {Gij} with marginals Pi,Qj exactly when every Pi commutes with every Qj; then Gij=PiQj.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: From 0≤Gij≤Pi derive Gij=PiGijPi by positive square root and kernel inclusion; sum over j and i to show PiQj=Gij.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Input a finite POVM {Fa} spanning the real Hermitian d×d matrices and frequencies fa≥0 summing to one; compute Gram G_ab=tr(FaFb), its Moore-Penrose inverse, dual Da=∑b(G+)ab Fb and output X=∑a fa Da. X is Hermitian with exact reconstruction for model probabilities; positivity is not imposed.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For n independent Bernoulli(p) variables and f their average, P(|f−p|≥t)≤2 exp(−2nt²), t>0.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Convexity bounds the centered one-variable log moment generating function by s²/8: its second derivative is a Bernoulli variance at most 1/4, and its value and derivative at zero vanish. Sum the bounds, use Markov, optimize s=4t, and apply both tails.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For the spanning POVM procedure, exact probabilities pa=tr(ρFa) recover ρ. A deterministic frequency error gives ||X−ρ||₂≤||D||_(ℓ²→HS)||f−p||₂. For n IID samples and m outcomes, with probability≥1−δ every |fa−pa|≤sqrt(log(2m/δ)/(2n)).
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Prove frame reconstruction by Gram pseudoinverse on its range; use Hoeffding for each indicator and union bound. IID and the true POVM are declared statistical assumptions.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: A selected finite system and environment use a product initial state ρ⊗η and declared unitary U(t); reduced dynamics is Φt(ρ)=TrE U(t)(ρ⊗η)U(t)*. A time homogeneous GKSL model is a separately selected approximation with specified rates; it is not automatic from unitary reduction.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Physical assignment and validity regime, not a proof of Markovianity.

new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Diagonalize η=∑pk|k⟩⟨k| and use Kjk=√pk⟨j|U|k⟩; prove Kraus normalization. Give finite recurrent dephasing counterexample.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For an adopted qubit GKSL model H=ℏω|1⟩⟨1| and L=√γ|0⟩⟨1|, γ≥0 in s^−1, populations satisfy ρ11(t)=e^−γtρ11(0) and ρ01(t)=e^(iωt−γt/2)ρ01(0).
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Insert matrix units into the existing GKSL generator, solve linear ODEs and use published sufficient theorem for CPTP. No derivation from a vacuum continuum is claimed.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a finite GKSL generator with bounded jump operators, the no-jump contraction K(t)=exp[t(−iH/ℏ−∑L*aLa/2)] and time-ordered jump products define positive trajectory weights whose summed ensemble equals e^(tL)ρ. The expansion converges in trace norm on finite time intervals.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Duhamel expansion of L=N+J, bound nth term by e^(t||N||)(t||J||)^n/n!, and trace-preserving total mass. This is an ensemble representation, not unique microscopic trajectories.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For r≥1 use bosonic Fock over C^r, quadratures R=(Q1,P1,…,Qr,Pr) with [Rj,Rk]=iℏJjk on finite Hermite span. A Gaussian state is specified by characteristic function χ(z)=tr ρ exp(i z·R)=exp(i z·d−zᵀVz/2), with real d and real symmetric V; finite second moments are required.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use the existing closed ladder domains and oscillator ON basis; define exponentials by the regular Weyl system, not by an unbounded formal series.

new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Decompose S into Fourier rotations, invertible coordinate changes and real quadratic chirps; prove each integral/unitary formula and its Weyl conjugation. Prove the decomposition with Gaussian elimination on Lagrangian blocks, including singular blocks. Use regular irreducibility for phase uniqueness.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For real symmetric positive definite 2r×2r V there is S symplectic and positive νj such that V=S diag(ν1,ν1,…,νr,νr) Sᵀ. The uncertainty condition is equivalent to every νj≥ℏ/2.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For any state with finite quadrature second moments, V+iℏJ/2≥0. Under an implemented symplectic transformation, d→Sd and V→SVSᵀ. For finite-mode Gaussian χ, this inequality is also sufficient for existence of a density operator with that characteristic function.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Necessity follows from ⟨C*C⟩≥0 for C=∑cj(Rj−dj); sufficiency requires the NEW Williamson diagonalization lemma below and product oscillator thermal states.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For m>0 and charge q, select the closed Friedrichs magnetic form qA[u]=(1/2m)∑||(-iℏ∂j−qAj)u||²+∫V|u|² on the closure of Cc∞ in its form norm, for smooth real A and real V∈L¹loc bounded below. A spin-half Pauli term −g q S·B/(2m) is an additional effective coupling with declared g and a semibounded realization.

Its spectrum is {ℏ|qB| (n+1/2)/m:n≥0}, each with infinite multiplicity and no continuous spectral measure.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: A charge q constrained to a circle radius R with flux Φ uses HΦ=(ℏ²/(2mR²))(−i∂φ−α)² on periodic H², α=qΦ/(2πℏ). Its energies are ℏ²(n−α)²/(2mR²), n∈Z, and Φ→Φ+2πℏk/q is unitarily equivalent.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: On Cc∞ spinors for smooth A, (σ·Π)²=Π²−qℏ σ·B with Π=−iℏ∇−qA. Therefore the quadratic Pauli Hamiltonian (σ·Π)²/(2m) gives g=2 at the formal-core level; its closed nonnegative form realization is selected separately.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For ℓ²(Z^d)⊗C^r and a finite-range translation-invariant Hermitian hopping operator (Hψ)n=∑δ Tδ ψ_(n−δ), T_(−δ)=Tδ*, define Fourier Bloch fibers h(k)=∑δ Tδ e^(−ik·δ), k∈T^d. An isolated group of bands defines the orthogonal spectral projector P(k).

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a C² gapped rank-r projector P(k) on the oriented two-torus, C=(i/2π)∫tr P dP∧dP is an integer, invariant under C² deformations preserving a uniform gap. A globally smooth periodic orthonormal frame forces C=0.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Apply the projector curvature theorem to the determinant line bundle; prove the determinant transition connection and integrate exact transgression under homotopy.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For smooth h(k)=d0(k)I+d(k)·σ with |d|>0 on T², the eigenprojectors P±=(I±n·σ)/2, n=d/|d|, satisfy C(P±)=∓(1/4π)∫n·(∂1n×∂2n)dk1dk2.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Expand tr(P[∂1P,∂2P]) with Pauli matrices and the fixed i/(2π) convention. Prove integer degree by regular-value/chart winding or invoke the explicitly supplied line-class argument.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For a wave packet in a simple smooth isolated band and an explicitly adopted slow-force single-band approximation, the effective Lagrangian L=ℏk·xdot+ iℏ u(k)*∂k u(k)·kdot−E(k)+q Eext·x gives ℏkdot=qEext and xdot=(1/ℏ)∇kE−kdot×Ω, with Ω the real Berry curvature in the matching convention.

Proving the wave-packet approximation error requires the semiclassical supplier and a new space-adiabatic theorem; this item claims only the conditional finite-dimensional variational consequence.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For continuous T-periodic Hermitian H(t) on C^d, U(t)=P(t)e^(−itHF/ℏ) with a Hermitian HF and T-periodic unitary P(t). HF is defined from a chosen Hermitian logarithm of U(T), and quasienergies are defined modulo 2πℏ/T.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Diagonalize U(T), select eigenphases and set HF; define P(t)=U(t)e^(itHF/ℏ), use periodic propagator composition.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For C¹ periodic finite Hermitian H(t), K=H(t)−iℏ∂t on L²(S¹_T)⊗C^d with periodic H¹ domain is self-adjoint as a bounded perturbation of the Fourier derivative. Its eigenvectors e^(inωt)P(t)vj have eigenvalues εj+nℏω.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use the explicit periodic derivative multiplier, Kato–Rellich and the Floquet normal form; verify the conjugating periodic unitary preserves H¹.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For finite Hermitian H and projection P, let HD=PHP+(I−P)H(I−P), V=H−HD. Then ||e^(−itH/ℏ)−e^(−itHD/ℏ)||≤|t| ||V||/ℏ. Consequently leakage from ran P is bounded by this number.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate e^(−i(t−s)H/ℏ)e^(−isHD/ℏ), integrate and use unitarity. No unbounded coupling estimate follows without domain control.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Input d, Fourier coefficients Hm with H_(−m)=Hm*, finite harmonic bandwidth b, ω>0 and cutoff N≥0; output the Hermitian matrix K_nm=H_(n−m)+nℏω δnm I for −N≤n,m≤N. Assemble blocks and diagonalize to requested numerical tolerance with a declared classical eigensolver.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Finite loops terminate after (2N+1)² block assignments; correctness means exact compression of the Sambe operator, not automatic convergence of all computed quasienergies.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: The specified Fourier–Galerkin assembly terminates after finitely many block operations and its exact output matrix is the orthogonal compression of K to harmonics −N,…,N; it is Hermitian. Numerical diagonalization accuracy is a separate residual claim.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Compute each Fourier matrix element of multiplication and derivative, use H_(−m)=Hm*, and count a finite square index set.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Input a semibounded closed form q, finite independent vectors φj∈Q(q), Gram matrix Gij=⟨φj,φi⟩ and form matrix Aij=q(φj,φi). Output eigenvalues and G-normalized coefficients of Ac=λGc after positive Gram factorization.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Define exact arithmetic procedure and required quadrature enclosure if entries are numerical; no hidden assumption that trial vectors lie in D(H).

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Each kth Rayleigh–Ritz value from an n-dimensional conforming form subspace is ≥ the kth min-max spectral value for k≤n, and nested dense form subspaces converge to every isolated eigenvalue below essential spectrum.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Restrict the min-max infimum and approximate a finite spectral eigenspace in the form norm; control its Gram matrix and energy uniformly.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: For self-adjoint H, normalized u∈D(H), real λ and r=(H−λ)u, dist(λ,σ(H))≤||r||. If all spectrum outside a selected cluster lies at distance≥g>0 from λ, then ||(I−Pcluster)u||≤||r||/g.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Let H be self-adjoint, v(t) a C¹ H-valued path with v(t)∈D(H), Hv continuous and r=iℏv′−Hv integrable. Then ||v(t)−e^(−itH/ℏ)v(0)||≤ℏ^−1∫0^|t| ||r(s)||ds with the corresponding oriented interval.
new_planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate the interaction-picture vector using the stated graph regularity, integrate the residual and apply unitarity.

new_planned_interfaces.interface: Select finitely many oscillator modes, a finite atomic Hilbert space and compressed dipole matrices. Specify mode frequencies, coupling constants and photon-count/homodyne POVMs. Long-wavelength, rotating-wave and Markov approximations are separate optional assumptions with named scale regimes.
